title: On-call and Incident Response Playbook - Rotations, Game Days, Runbooks and Communications
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Purpose:

This operational playbook documents Redwood Inference's day-to-day on-call and incident response practices with emphasis on rotations, runbook usage, postmortems, game days, and customer communications. It is intended to be a practical reference for on-call engineers, SREs, and engineering managers.

Quick summary of responsibilities:
- Primary on-call: first responder, triage, initial mitigation, and internal updates.
- Secondary on-call: escalation support and cross-team coordination.
- SRE Pager: infra-level mitigations (networking, capacity, cloud accounts).
- Communications lead: owns status page and external notifications.

Incident classification:
- Sev1 (Critical): total service outage, control plane unavailable, data corruption, or confirmed security incident with customer impact. Immediate page + exec alert.
- Sev2 (High): degraded service causing significant customer impact (error rate > 10% across routes or latency > 5x baseline for > 5 minutes).
- Sev3 (Medium): partial degradation, single-customer incident, or intermittent errors.
- Sev4 (Low): informational or non-urgent operational issues.

Incident lifecycle (detailed):
1) Detection and alerting: Prometheus/Datadog -> Alertmanager -> PagerDuty. Alerts must include runbook link when available.
2) Acknowledge (T+2 minutes target): primary on-call acknowledges and posts an initial note to #incidents.
3) Triage (T+0 to T+20 minutes): scope (regions, customers), confirm severity, capture key traces and metrics, and determine mitigation plan.
4) Mitigation (T+0 to T+60 minutes): apply short-term mitigations, e.g., route to fallback model, scale GPU pool, restart faulty nodes.
5) Communications (continuous): update internal channel and status page per cadence.
6) Resolution verification: confirm stable metrics for 30 minutes and mark incident resolved.
7) Postmortem: draft within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2; finalize within two weeks with action items and owners.

Runbook usage and template:
- Runbooks must be written for all common failure modes: model-router failures, KV cache thrash, GPU pool exhaustion, control-plane outages, deploy rollbacks.
- Template fields: title; service; owner_team; severity; trigger alerts; impact; prerequisites; mitigation steps; verification steps; post-incident follow-ups.

Example runbook excerpt (model-router high error rate):
1. Confirm alert and gather first 10 error traces from Datadog.
2. Check recent deploys: Review CI/CD deploy dashboard and `kubectl rollout status` for inference services.
3. Check model routing: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.internal/api/routing/current?service=inference`
4. Switch traffic to fallback model: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.internal/api/routing -d '{"target":"model-v0"}'`
5. If backend nodes show OOMs, cycle pods on unhealthy nodes: `kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl delete pod $POD -n inference`
6. If control-plane impact suspected, follow control-plane-failover runbook.

Verification: check p95 latency and error rate return to baseline for 30 minutes; confirm traces show success paths.

Escalation policy and contacts:
- PagerDuty escalation: primary -> 10 minutes -> secondary -> 15 minutes -> SRE lead -> Engineering Director.
- For Sev1 incidents: notify Eng Director and Product Operations immediately.
- Quick contacts: Miguel Rivera (SRE lead), Asha Patel (Eng Director). Emails and PagerDuty contacts are in the team roster.

On-call rotations and health:
- Standard cadence: 1-week rotations for primary and secondary on-call.
- Limits: max 3 consecutive weeks primary; minimum 48 hours rest between rotations.
- Handoff: post a summary in #incidents, link to dashboards, and confirm no active todo items. If active incident, conduct a 5-minute verbal handoff.
- Coverage for vacations: on-call manager arranges backfill.

Game days (exercise program):
- Purpose: validate runbooks, test failovers and capacity limits, and improve cross-team coordination.
- Frequency: quarterly per team, annual company-wide.
- Typical scenarios: GPU pool disruption, model-router regression, cross-region network partition.
- Reporting: game day report with findings and action items due within 7 days.

Postmortem policy and template:
- Required for all Sev1/Sev2 incidents with customer impact and for repeated Sev3 incidents.
- Timeline: initial summary in-channel within 8 hours; draft postmortem within 72 hours; final within 2 weeks.
- Template fields: incident id; timeframe; services affected; timeline; root cause; mitigating actions; remediation plan; owners; verification steps; lessons learned.

Example action items:
- Add circuit-breaker to model-router (owner: eng-serving-runtime, due: 2026-03-15).
- Harden cache eviction logic and add unit tests (owner: applied-ml-and-evals, due: 2026-03-01).
- Add synthetic traffic monitors for fallback-model discovery (owner: eng-platform, due: 2026-02-28).

Status page and customer communications:
- Use the public status page for customer-visible incidents (Sev1/Sev2). Update cadence: every 30 minutes for Sev1, every 60 minutes for Sev2.
- Send targeted emails to high-touch customers for incidents that affect them, following the templates below.

Customer email templates (use as basis):
1) Initial customer acknowledgement (within 30 minutes):
Subject: Redwood Inference - Incident affecting <service> in <region>
Body: Hello <Customer>,
We are investigating an issue affecting <service> in <region> that may impact inference requests. Our on-call team is triaging and we will provide an update by <ETA>. For urgent inquiries contact your account team.

2) Mitigation update:
Subject: Update - Incident affecting <service> in <region>
Body: Hello <Customer>,
We have applied a mitigation: <brief summary>. We are monitoring impact and expect next update by <ETA>.

3) Resolution notice:
Subject: Resolved - Incident affecting <service> in <region>
Body: Hello <Customer>,
The incident was resolved at <time>. Root cause: <short summary>. Actions taken and next steps: <list>. A postmortem will be shared in <X days>. Contact your account team for follow-up.

Communications roles and templates:
- Communications lead posts status updates and sends customer emails.
- Engineering lead provides technical summaries for status updates.
- Use incident Zoom template for live comms; include link in #incidents.

Maintenance and ownership:
- Playbook owner: eng-sre. Service teams (eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, applied-ml-and-evals) own their runbooks and must review them quarterly.
- Change process: update the runbook page, request reviewer approvals, and include a changelog entry with date and summary.

Appendices:
- Useful CLI commands: `kubectl get pods -n inference`, `kubectl describe pod $POD -n inference`, `kubectl logs -f $POD -n inference`
- Dashboards: Inference API Overview (Datadog), GPU pool capacity (internal link), Routing and failover metrics (internal link).
- Links: postmortem-template, runbook-library, game-day-checklist.

If you find gaps in runbooks or see recurring alerts without a runbook, please open an issue on the eng-sre board and notify the on-call manager.
